related_questions.question: What is a rare autoimmune disease that attacks muscles?

text_blocks.snippet: Several rare autoimmune diseases can cause muscle weakness or damage, including dermatomyositis, polymyositis, and myasthenia gravis. These conditions involve the immune system mistakenly attacking muscle tissue, leading to a range of symptoms from mild weakness to severe muscle damage and potentially life-threatening complications.

list.title: Dermatomyositis:
list.snippet: A rare autoimmune disease that primarily affects muscles and skin, causing inflammation and muscle weakness.

list.title: Polymyositis:
list.snippet: Another rare autoimmune disease characterized by muscle weakness, particularly in the proximal muscles (shoulders, hips).

list.title: Myasthenia Gravis:
list.snippet: A rare autoimmune neuromuscular disease where the immune system attacks the connection between nerves and muscles, leading to muscle weakness and fatigue.

list.title: Neuromyotonia:
list.snippet: A rare disorder where the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves, causing muscle twitching, cramping, and stiffness, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome:
list.snippet: While not solely focused on muscle tissue, this syndrome can cause muscle weakness and paralysis due to immune system attack on the peripheral nervous system.

list.title: Inclusion Body Myositis:
list.snippet: A progressive muscle disorder characterized by muscle weakness and atrophy, often affecting older adults.
Muscle weakness: A common symptom, ranging from mild to severe.
Fatigue: Muscle weakness can lead to fatigue and reduced physical endurance.
Inflammation: Inflammation of muscle tissue is a key feature of many of these conditions.
Autoimmune origin: The diseases are caused by the immune system mistakenly attacking the body's own tissues.
Rare occurrence: These conditions are generally considered rare, with varying prevalence depending on the specific disease.
Diagnosis often involves blood tests to check for elevated muscle enzymes and autoantibodies, as well as muscle biopsies and neurological assessments.
Treatment options vary depending on the specific disease and its severity, but may include immunosuppressant drugs, physical therapy, and other supportive measures.

text_blocks.snippet: A disease of the muscle, also known as myopathy, can manifest in various forms, ranging from inherited conditions like muscular dystrophy to acquired disorders such as myositis. These diseases can lead to muscle weakness, pain, and atrophy, impacting movement and overall physical function.

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of common muscle diseases:

list.snippet: A group of genetic diseases characterized by progressive muscle weakness and degeneration.
Different types affect various muscle groups and progress at different rates.
Examples include Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Becker muscular dystrophy, and FSHD.
Symptoms can include muscle weakness, difficulty walking, breathing problems, and heart issues.
Inflammatory muscle diseases that can be autoimmune or caused by infections or medications.
Polymyositis, dermatomyositis, and inclusion body myositis are some forms.
Symptoms include muscle weakness, pain, and fatigue.
Treatment often involves corticosteroids and immunosuppressants.
Caused by genetic defects affecting the body's metabolism, impacting muscle function.
Examples include mitochondrial myopathies and glycogen storage diseases.
Symptoms vary depending on the specific condition and can include muscle weakness, pain, and exercise intolerance.
Encompass conditions affecting the nerves, muscles, or the communication between them.
Can lead to muscle weakness, atrophy, and sensory disturbances.
Includes conditions like ALS, myasthenia gravis, and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
Wasting or thinning of muscle mass, which can be caused by disuse, nerve damage, or other conditions.
Symptoms include decreased muscle mass, limb weakness, and numbness.
Can be reversed with exercise and a healthy diet in some cases.
Muscle damage caused by exposure to toxins, medications, or drugs.
Symptoms can include muscle weakness, pain, and cramps.
Treatment involves removing the offending agent.
Myasthenia Gravis: An autoimmune disorder causing muscle weakness, particularly in the face and limbs.
Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS): A neurodegenerative disease affecting motor neurons, leading to muscle weakness and paralysis.
